leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of the eight round-1 files state a preferred configuration consisting of B030 alone, with Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye as the two laureates. Four of the seven (Danielsson, Johansson, Olsson, Pearce) moved to B030 from a different opening first choice; Kroll, Lindroth and Mehlig held it first. Eriksson is the one member who does not list B030 as preferred: he prefers B022 (Parrinello and Car) alone, names B030 as his first alternative, and says he would not stand in the way of B030 or B058 on the merits and would defer to Lindroth and Kroll on technical priority. What the seven share is the two-name allocation, the description of the invention as the magic-wavelength proposal plus its realization near 1e-18, and the view that independent laboratory agreement establishes maturity. What is not shared is how much weight the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 metrology prizes deserves, whether the lack of credit to other lattice-clock groups matters, and how the pending redefinition of the second should enter the case. The citation wordings also differ in scope, from a bare 'invention and realization of optical lattice clocks' (Olsson) to wording that names the 10^-18 level or the magic wavelength.

areas_of_agreement: Seven members (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) explicitly prefer B030 alone, credited to Katori and Ye, and Eriksson names B030 as his first alternative; no file proposes a second prize part or a third laureate for B030.

Members who comment on the B030 attribution (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) call the two-name credit the cleanest, or among the cleanest, on the shortlist, while Eriksson makes the same claim for B022.
Members who comment on maturity say that independent laboratories in several countries have reproduced fractional uncertainties near 1e-18.
Kroll, Lindroth, Johansson, Olsson and Pearce say the B030 citation should rest on the invention and its realization and not on the redefinition of the second, which has not yet occurred.
Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce each state that B029 should not displace B030 now, citing the missing Wallraff and the 2025 prize on neighbouring superconducting-circuit physics.
Several members (Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce) describe B020 as a genuine discovery of a new observational window, while several of them judge its attribution unsettled.
scientific_disputes: Whether the 2005 prize (frequency comb) and the 2012 prize (control of single trapped ions) leave room for a lattice-clock award. Lindroth, Kroll, Olsson and Pearce argue the magic-wavelength lattice is a distinct idea neither prize covered. Mehlig says the overlap in method is close enough that it should not be treated as closed. Danielsson, Johansson and Pearce list it as their strongest reservation.

Whether the clock is a discovery or an invention whose payoff is mainly technological. Danielsson says the discovery content has to be argued through tests of gravitational redshift, varying constants and dark matter, and Lindroth, Kroll and Mehlig reply that the light-shift, forbidden-transition and many-body physics is itself the achievement.

Whether a computational method (B022, Car and Parrinello) counts as a physics discovery or invention or sits with chemistry. Eriksson and Mehlig raise it; Johansson, Kroll and Lindroth say it is unresolved and rank it below B030. Only Eriksson and Mehlig rank B022 in their top eight.

Whether the invention criterion extends to instrument and device entries (B025 electron optics, B008 quantum cascade laser). Olsson argues it does; Eriksson replies that these carry credit problems of their own, and no member other than Olsson ranked B025.
For B004, whether atom-in-optical-lattice simulation is mainly a simulator whose promise for real materials is still being established (Eriksson) or a new route to correlated matter (Kroll).
attribution_disputes: B030: Katori for the magic-wavelength proposal and early demonstrations, Ye for record accuracy, many-body clock physics and comparison technology. Pearce asks that this be called a judgement and not a clean fact. Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and the ion-clock groups are named as contributors outside the credited pair. Lindroth would not name Lemonde in the citation, and Olsson regards Lemonde and others as contested rather than clearly excluded.

B020: the split among Halzen, Karle and Spiering, and between the AMANDA founders, the IceCube leaders and the collaboration. Pearce lists Halzen, Karle and Spiering; Danielsson names Halzen and Karle with the third place left open; Johansson names Karle, Spiering and Halzen. Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Johansson say the credit among conception, construction and analysis is not settled.

B004: no trio of Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger is accepted by everyone. Kroll and Pearce drop Greiner, Danielsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson drop Esslinger, Eriksson drops Zoller, and Jaksch is not in the credited names. Kroll says he would not defend his own trio against Bloch, Greiner and Zoller.
B029: the credited trio omits Wallraff, who carried out the 2004 strong-coupling experiment, and the Yale, ETH and Sherbrooke contributions cannot be separated in three names.
B017: five credited names, including the LHC machine and the ATLAS and CMS leadership, cannot be reduced to three without an arbitrary cut (Pearce).
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the redefinition of the second. Kroll, Johansson, Olsson, Lindroth and Pearce would not tie the prize to it, and Eriksson says it will not change the science. Danielsson lists it as an open uncertainty and Mehlig says it affects how much practical impact is already realised.
B020: the diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux is treated as secure, but Danielsson, Johansson and Kroll note that the origin of most of it is unresolved, which they weigh against its maturity.
B029: timing so soon after the 2025 prize on neighbouring superconducting-circuit physics (Danielsson, Johansson, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce).
B004: Eriksson says the promise for real materials is still being established.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Eriksson (B022): works in electronic-structure theory and atomistic simulation at Uppsala, the field of B022, and says this may call for recusal or at least disclosure on B022. No tie to Car or Parrinello is recorded.

Johansson (B029): circuit QED is his own research area, he is at Chalmers and director of WACQT, and he states he should be recused from weighing B029. He lists documented ties to Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson and to Anton Frisk Kockum, and says no connection to B030 or B004 is apparent.

Kroll (B030): spent a research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, the lineage from which Jun Ye's group at JILA developed. He reports no direct collaboration, supervisory or institutional tie to Katori or Ye and flags the field proximity for B004 (Zoller) as well. He sees no recusal need.

Olsson (B025): B025 is in her own field of transmission electron microscopy and she would consider recusing herself from a final decision on it. For B030 she mentions exchanges with Japanese universities, including a University of Tokyo fellowship, with no specific connection to Katori or Ye.

Lindroth: flags general professional proximity to precision atomic physics and to ETH and Lund experimental groups, and asks the chair to decide whether recusal is required. No collaborator is among the B030 names.

Pearce (chair, B020): flags subject proximity through astroparticle work on PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, PoGOLite/PoGO+ and XL-Calibur, with no recorded tie to the credited names, and does not claim a recusal-level conflict. B020 is his first alternative, not his preferred part.
Danielsson, Mehlig: state that no specific conflict is apparent from their profiles for the shortlisted candidates they discuss.
questions_for_round2: The committee must state in one sentence why lattice clocks are a distinct achievement from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes. Can members who hold the overlap worry (Danielsson, Mehlig, Johansson, Pearce) say whether that sentence would resolve it, or whether the overlap remains disqualifying for them?

Should the B030 citation be written around the magic-wavelength lattice invention and its realization, and not around optical clocks or timekeeping in general? Which of the three citation scopes in the round-1 files (the bare invention-and-realization wording, wording naming the 10^-18 level, or wording naming the magic wavelength) does each member support?

Is the Katori and Ye allocation defensible against the contributions of Lemonde, Lisdat, Ludlow and the ion-clock groups? What evidence beyond the supplied text would members need to see that the two-name allocation holds, and would any member change the pair?
Does any member now argue that the pending redefinition of the second should delay the award? If not, can the committee record that the case rests on demonstrated performance alone?

If B030 were set aside, which single alternative would each member support? The first alternatives are split: B004 (Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce), B058 (Eriksson, Kroll, Lindroth), B020 (Danielsson, Pearce), B029 (Johansson), B022 (Mehlig), B025 and B008 (Olsson), B030 (Eriksson).

For B004 and B020, which three-name allocation, if any, would the proponents defend? In particular, can Danielsson and Pearce agree on Spiering for B020, and can Kroll and Pearce accept Greiner in B004?

Eriksson prefers B022 alone while saying he would not oppose B030. Does he now support B030 as the single prize part, or does he hold B022 as a competing configuration, and would the committee treat B022 as a physics invention? Separately, would members with disclosed proximity (Eriksson on B022, Johansson on B029, Olsson on B025) take part in weighing those entries if they enter a configuration?
summary.chair_observation: Seven of eight members state B030 alone as their preferred round-1 configuration, and Eriksson, who prefers B022, names it as his first alternative. Four of the seven reached B030 after moving from another opening first choice. Every member who supports it states a reservation about prize overlap, secondary credit or the pending redefinition of the second. Behind B030 the alternatives are scattered (B004, B058, B020, B029, B022, B025, B008), and each of them has an unresolved credit or scope question that round 2 has not yet tested.
